tagline: North through the last slave state, by way of Quaker meetinghouses.
intro: The Delaware leg starts on Willow Grove Road in Kent County, where Maryland's Tubman byway leaves off, and runs north through Camden, Dover, Smyrna, Middletown and Odessa. Then Route 9 follows the Delaware River up to Wilmington, and Kennett Pike carries it out to the Pennsylvania line.

Delaware was the last slave state on the way north. In Wilmington the Quaker hardware merchant Thomas Garrett kept his station so openly that his house on Shipley Street needed no secret rooms, and Harriet Tubman passed through it many times. He said he had "only helped 2,700."

moments.title: Appoquinimink Friends Meetinghouse
moments.text: The little Odessa meetinghouse, built about 1785 and only about 20 by 22 feet, has a removable panel in its loft under the eaves that may have hidden freedom seekers.

moments.title: New Castle Court House
moments.text: Fined into ruin here in 1848, Thomas Garrett told the court to send him any fugitive who needed a friend, under the cupola that centers the 12-mile circle of the Pennsylvania line.

moments.title: Tubman-Garrett Riverfront Park
moments.text: On the Christina River across from Wilmington's train station, a bronze of Tubman, Garrett and two freedom seekers has stood since 2012.
